features.evidence: 7 years at Amazon testing, maintaining, and launching 6 production services
features.name: Production experience scale
features.description: Captures the amount of substantial software-product experience evidenced through years in role and repeated launches of production services.

levels.descriptor: Little concrete production scope is stated, or the experience described is minimal and unclear.
Meets baseline expectations but shows limited scope, such as only a few years in industry or only one or two clearly owned services.
Shows solid early-to-mid-career production experience with multiple services and credible testing, maintenance, and launch exposure.
Shows strong production scope, typically with about five or more years and several services launched or operated.
Shows extensive production experience with long tenure and repeated service ownership or launches across multiple systems.

features.name: Academic training level
features.description: Captures the highest degree level explicitly claimed, which is a stated preferred qualification for the role.

levels.descriptor: No advanced degree beyond a bachelor's degree is stated, or degree level is unclear.
A master's degree or equivalent advanced graduate training is stated.
A doctoral degree or equivalent research-intensive terminal degree is stated.

features.evidence: Python became my workhorse for everything operational
features.name: Python implementation depth
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter shows Python as a real implementation language rather than a box-check.

levels.descriptor: Python is not mentioned or is only implied.
Python is mentioned generically, usually for scripts or light tooling, with little detail.
The letter clearly shows hands-on Python use in services, tooling, automation, or analysis that mattered to the team.
The letter shows strong production-grade Python depth, such as typed or tested services, broadly used tooling, or central automation work.

features.evidence: shipping model-integrated functionality wrapped in the checks that make it dependable
features.name: AI production maturity
features.description: Captures whether the letter shows practical experience deploying AI systems responsibly, especially with reliability or evaluation concerns.

levels.descriptor: No AI or LLM experience is mentioned.
AI experience is mentioned vaguely, with no clear production use or reliability detail.
The letter describes shipping AI-backed features or workflows in production.
The letter shows shipped AI work plus concrete attention to trustworthiness, evaluation, guardrails, or failure modes.

features.evidence: Python agents with clear contracts, Go infrastructure that makes their boundaries impossible to wander past
features.name: Agentic tooling design
features.description: Captures experience designing systems where agents act autonomously under explicit architectural controls.

levels.descriptor: No agentic or autonomous-system design is mentioned.
Agents are mentioned, but the letter gives little sense of architecture, control, or ownership.
The letter clearly describes building agentic tooling with distinct agent and service roles.
The letter shows end-to-end agent architecture with explicit permissions, supervision, auditing, or guardrails.

features.evidence: turned an unstructured queue into a routed, prioritized pipeline
features.name: Vulnerability-triage automation
features.description: Captures direct experience automating the intake, classification, routing, or deduplication of vulnerability reports.

levels.descriptor: No direct vulnerability-handling automation is described.
The letter expresses interest in reducing security toil but gives no concrete automation example.
The letter describes some vulnerability-handling automation in general terms.
The letter gives a clear hands-on example of triage automation that classifies, routes, or deduplicates reports.
The letter shows strong, outcome-oriented triage automation with clear operational impact or notably sophisticated workflow design.

features.evidence: threat models and follow-through, not just a checklist and a signature
features.name: Security assessment depth
features.description: Captures whether the letter demonstrates real security review work, from threat modeling to code review and remediation.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment experience is claimed.
Assessments or reviews are mentioned vaguely, with little method, scope, or ownership.
The letter describes concrete assessment work such as threat modeling, code review, validating fixes, or formal reviews.
The letter shows strong assessment maturity, such as leading reviews, assessing systems the applicant did not build, or treating assessments as substantive engineering deliverables.

features.evidence: made an intractable dedup problem boringly fast
features.name: Algorithmic problem-solving
features.description: Captures whether the letter provides credible evidence of data-structures-and-algorithms fluency applied to real systems.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic evidence is given beyond generic claims or preferred-qualification matching.
The letter claims strength in algorithms or data structures but provides little concrete proof.
The letter gives a specific example of using better structures or algorithms to improve a system.
The letter gives a strong, technically credible example where algorithmic thinking materially changed performance, tractability, or bug rate.

features.evidence: I took the OSCP certification because I wanted my offensive skills examined the hard way
features.name: Security certification strength
features.description: Captures whether the letter offers formal security credentials and how practice-oriented they are.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A fundamentals-oriented credential such as Security+ is mentioned.
A hands-on credential such as OSCP, or an equivalently practice-heavy certification, is mentioned.

features.evidence: top placements in several large open competitions
features.name: Offensive practice intensity
features.description: Captures the seriousness and demonstrated level of capture-the-flag or similar adversarial security practice.

levels.descriptor: No CTF or adversarial practice is mentioned.
Participation is mentioned casually or occasionally, with no indication of level.
The letter presents regular CTF participation as deliberate skill-building.
The letter gives a strong competitive signal, such as serious involvement or near-top or top placements.

features.evidence: maintain an open-source project with a real community around it
features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures whether the letter shows responsibility for code used beyond the applicant's immediate job, from patches to project maintenance.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional upstream patches or fixes.
The letter shows ongoing maintenance of a small project or recurring upstream responsibility.
The letter shows sustained stewardship of an open-source project with users, releases, reviews, or community responsibility.

features.evidence: a fault-tolerant message broker from scratch, with consensus and recovery logic
features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures how technically stretching and self-directed the applicant's outside projects appear.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
The project mentioned is small and mainly serves as lightweight practice or curiosity.
The project shows substantial self-directed engineering with meaningful system design or operational concerns.
The project is an ambitious systems build that tackles hard distributed-systems, storage, or reliability problems.

features.evidence: improvements there are inherited by every team downstream
features.name: Platform leverage mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames impact in terms of foundational infrastructure and organization-wide leverage.

levels.descriptor: No clear platform or foundation-level motivation is expressed.
The letter mentions impact or scale in generic terms without much platform framing.
The letter clearly prefers foundational work whose benefits spread across teams or products.
The letter strongly and repeatedly articulates central-platform leverage as a core reason for wanting the role.

features.evidence: helping busy developer teams do the secure thing by default
features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter sees security engineering as enabling product teams through better defaults, tooling, and workflows.

levels.descriptor: No explicit developer-enablement framing appears.
The letter shows a general desire to help teams, but not specifically through security workflows or defaults.
The letter clearly states that security should assist developers rather than merely police them.
The letter shows a strong secure-by-default philosophy with empathy for busy engineers and attention to embedding good behavior into everyday workflows.

features.name: Security-automation systems thinking
features.description: Captures whether the letter understands the role as scaling scarce security expertise through principled automation rather than isolated scripts.

levels.descriptor: No broader framing of security automation is given.
Automation is mentioned mainly as convenience or efficiency, without a systems view.
The letter clearly frames automation as reducing toil or scaling team output.
The letter shows strategic understanding of capacity multiplication, centralizing scarce judgment, or variant-analysis-style leverage.

features.evidence: someone always inherits what we build
features.name: Maintainer orientation
features.description: Captures whether the letter emphasizes maintainability, operational humility, and long-term ownership rather than just feature shipping.

levels.descriptor: No explicit maintainer or long-term-ownership mindset is shown.
The letter hints at care or reliability, but without a clear ownership philosophy.
The letter clearly describes learning from maintenance, operations, inherited systems, or durable ownership.
The letter presents a strong maintainer identity centered on reliability, inheritance, and disciplined long-term stewardship.

features.evidence: measured its worth in the hours of expert attention it returned to the team
features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how concrete and outcome-bearing the letter's examples are, as opposed to generic assertions of fit.

levels.descriptor: The letter is mostly generic, paraphrases the posting, or makes unsupported claims.
The letter includes some examples, but they remain broad and mostly assertive rather than demonstrative.
The letter offers several concrete examples of systems, tasks, or responsibilities.
The letter gives specific, credible examples tied to technical decisions, impact, or operational stakes.
The letter repeatedly grounds claims in detailed achievements, design choices, and clear outcomes or measured effect.

features.evidence: Every security team I have seen has the same bottleneck: too many signals, too few experts
features.name: Role-specific motivation
features.description: Captures how convincingly the letter explains why this particular security-engineering role matters to the applicant.

levels.descriptor: The motivation is formulaic and could fit almost any software-engineering application.
The letter shows some interest in security or Google, but the rationale is still fairly generic.
The letter gives clear, role-relevant motivation tied to the team's mission, working model, or problem space.
The letter gives memorable, well-tailored motivation that shows the applicant has thought specifically about this team's security-automation challenge.

features.name: Writing mechanics
features.description: Captures the amount of distracting spelling or copy-editing error in the letter.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors repeatedly interrupt reading or noticeably weaken professionalism.
Several visible errors appear, though the letter remains understandable.
Only a few minor slips appear and they do not materially distract.
The copy is clean or nearly clean, with strong proofreading and little to no noticeable error burden.
